title: Leibniz University Hannover Launches €5.8 Million ($6.53 Million USD) HybriQCS Project to Develop Hybrid Molecule-Rydberg Quantum Systems - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Leibniz University Hannover’s Kai Voges launched the 5-year, EUR 5.8M BMFTR-funded HybriQCS project to combine ultracold polar molecules (long-lived memory) with Rydberg atoms (fast gates), targeting the first two-qubit gate between the two by early 2031.

insights.claim: The HybriQCS project at Leibniz University Hannover has EUR 5.8 million (about $6.5M) from Germany’s BMFTR under its Quantum Futur early-career competition, running March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2031.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modest public funding for a long-horizon platform bet; no commercial near-term impact.

insights.claim: The project’s primary target is the first two-qubit quantum logic gate operation combining ultracold molecules and Rydberg excitation states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A milestone to watch in the 2028-2031 window; not yet demonstrated according to the article’s framing.

insights.claim: The architecture pairs ultracold polar molecules as quantum memory, with coherence lasting seconds to minutes because of weak environmental coupling, with Rydberg atoms that provide fast gate speeds and long-range entangling interactions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid memory-plus-processor designs are an alternative route to the coherence/speed trade-off; compare with mainstream neutral-atom approaches from Pasqal and QuEra.

insights.claim: The team is also exploring dual-species optical atomic clocks that cross-reference clock transitions between molecules and neutral atoms to cancel common-mode optical noise and yield low-noise frequency standards.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A sensing/timing spin-off path that could precede computing applications.

insights.claim: The group operates inside Quantum Valley Lower Saxony and the QuantumFrontiers Cluster of Excellence, collaborates with trapped-ion groups at PTB, and is assessing commercial spin-off pathways for hybrid hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Part of Germany’s regional quantum cluster strategy; spin-offs are a possibility rather than a plan.
